per_finding.finding: R2-CL-01 (major): K3 pruning summary wrong for the 80% build; rests on single prompts
per_finding.note: Re-read the pipenetwork REAP80, mlx-community reap160, mgoin and Nota cards. REAP80 answers 'The capital of France is' with 'Paris.' and then drifts into a list; its Chinese prompt loops. It runs at 5.54 tok/s on a 512 GiB M3 Ultra, and the calibration mix is 40/30/15/15. reap160 (82% pruned, 2-bit) loops on the France prompt, reports perplexity and benchmarks as 'not done', has 51.7% router demand at 160 experts against 77.5% at 376, and top-k 16 to 6 did not help. Section 1, K6, K7, 3c and G1 all match these cards, and 'keep their coding ability' is gone. Nit: the K3 50% REAP row comes from Nota's card (Nota evaluated a REAP baseline), so 'the makers' evaluations' is loose for REAP.

per_finding.finding: R2-CL-02 (major): 5.85-10.6 GB/s stated as fact; 2.82x/1.93x called speedups
per_finding.note: SSD-LLaMA section 5.2 confirmed. 2.82x and 1.93x are read-bandwidth ratios; decode is 1.35-3.44x over llama.cpp and 1.57-15.61x over KTransformers. The flash-moe CLAUDE.md gives 2.41 ms for K=4 experts and about a 71% hit rate, which implies about 3.4 GB/s. Recomputed K2 at B=3.4: 1.51-2.24 tok/s with other work stopped and 0.85-1.05 today, so the dossier's 1.5-2.2 and 0.9-1.0 hold. A5, section 1, K2 and G2 label the range an assumption. Residual: section 1 line 91 calls the range 'SSD-LLaMA's 43-78% of peak', but 43.2% is the paper's best baseline, not SSD-LLaMA (A5 states this correctly).

per_finding.finding: R2-CL-03 (major): GSQ called CUDA-only; GGUF K-quant route and full-node need omitted
per_finding.note: Paper section 4.4, Appendix E and Tables 4, 13 and 14, plus the GSQ README, confirm the claims. The GGUF route starts from Unsloth K-quants and keeps the format. It 'runs unchanged on llama.cpp / Ollama' and is tested only on Qwen3-8B (Table 4) and Qwen3-4B (Table 13: Q2_K 35.01 to 48.34). The README lists Kimi-K2 at 8x H100/H200 (full node) minimum, and K2.5 at a full node, typically 1-2 nodes. Section 1, K2b, 3a, 3c, section 4 and G1 route (c) are correct. Table 14 names UD-IQ1_M at 2.4 bits against GSQ at 2.37 bits. Side effect not handled: Table 14 is task data for a Kimi GGUF, which contradicts section 1's 'GGUF files have only fidelity data' (see section 1 problems).

per_finding.note: mgoin card: 34.4200 / 68.2335 / 95.5269, 5-shot, 256-token limit, same harness and seed, ranked by router weight with no calibration. section1_problems: Line 34, 'A 700B-class model already runs on this Mac by streaming': not supported for Kevin's Mac. The GLM 5.3 numbers come from the ds4 maintainer's 128 GB M5 Max, whose SSD size is unknown. Section 5's disk table marks the 211.1 GB file 'no' for today's 203 GB free (153 GB usable), and section 1 itself says no 2 TB M5 Max has been tested. Write 'on a 128 GB M5 Max like this one' and add the disk condition.

Lines 97-98, 'The GGUF files have only fidelity data' and 'The only task results are for GSQ at 2.13 bits (294 GB)': row K2b contradicts this. It reports AgentBench scores for Unsloth's Kimi K2.5 UD-IQ1_M GGUF at 2.4 bits (40/61/39/41/47, GSQ paper Table 14) and for GSQ at 2.37 bits, not 2.13. K4 and 3c also give task numbers for REAP50+INT4 (about 2.25 bits per original expert weight). Section 3a Limits (line 437, 'None exist for the GGUF or MLX files a Mac would run') has the same error. The GSQ authors also note that GGUF evaluation was hampered by templating failures, which bears on the 'lower bound' reading.

Line 122, 'Stock mmap reaches about 2 GB/s, about 500 ms per GB': stated as fact, but the body (A5) only says 'I use about 2 GB/s', with no source. The only Mac evidence, flash-moe's '5x slower than pread' against a pread rate of about 3.4 GB/s, points lower, so the mmap estimate on line 90 (0.5-1.4 tok/s) may be optimistic. Label it an assumption, as was done for 5.85-10.6.

Line 91, 'SSD-LLaMA's 43-78% of peak': 43.2% is the best baseline in the SSD-LLaMA paper, not SSD-LLaMA itself. A5 (lines 195-196) states this correctly; section 1 should say '43% (best baseline) to 78% (SSD-LLaMA)'.
Line 34, 'Two community reports exist': S51 also reports Kimi K2.5 running in 96 GB of RAM on an M2 Max, with no speed given. Minor; the scoped wording on line 94 ('on a 128 GB Mac') is accurate.

Line 107, '(REAP or Nota; the makers' evaluations)': both 50% rows come from Nota's card, so the REAP 50% figures are Nota's evaluation of a REAP baseline, not the REAP build maker's. The 3c table has the same label. Minor.
Line 65, the quotation 'workload references, not a speed guarantee': accurate to ds4 SSD_STREAMING.md (S109), but the body never states it; section 3b lists other S109 guidance only. Info only.
verdict: The revision holds up. I re-opened the sources for all 23 round-2 findings: ds4 docs, GSQ paper and README, the K3, mgoin and ubicloud cards, AtomicChat JSONL, the oMLX runs, SSD-LLaMA, 2608.07911, 2609.04575, 2609.25809, Weschera, rita-aga, S51, Computerworld, MacDailyNews, the HF API and the main repo's S140. I also recomputed every changed number. 22 findings are fixed correctly. R2-CL-14 is only partly fixed: A5 still cites PetaPixel's 12.7 GB/s 'via S4', but MacDailyNews quotes only The Verge. The rejections and adjustments are all justified: the exact S120 'worst choice in that grid' quote, the 45-82 tok/s managed-cache prefill, and the kept h brackets and 1.4-3.0 tok/s today case. The headline is unchanged: Kimi on this Mac means slow streaming, and V4 Flash 0731 or GLM-5.3-Flash is the practical choice. Section 1 needs three corrections before it goes out. (1) 'Already runs on this Mac' overstates: the GLM 5.3 streaming result is the maintainer's M5 Max, and the 211 GB file does not fit Kevin's free disk today. (2) 'GGUF files have only fidelity data' and 'the only task results are GSQ 2.13-bit' are contradicted by the dossier's own K2b row (Unsloth K2.5 UD-IQ1_M AgentBench, GSQ Table 14); 3a Limits repeats the error. (3) The 2 GB/s mmap rate is stated as fact but is an unsourced assumption. Smaller residuals: section 1 calls 43-78% 'SSD-LLaMA's'; the section 5 disk table leaves the 156 GB MXFP4 file unnamed; S131's file could also be the Vision-Exp q2-q4 mix; the event-atomic inflation applies mainly when an event's expert set exceeds the per-layer quota, so its effect on S82's single-stream brackets is probably small.
